why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief, looking for PASS/FAIL conditions or probes that appear in both. None of the verifier's own methods appear in the builder brief. These are the `cmp` and `<(printf …)` byte comparisons, `od -c`, `grep -rn -- '--tsv' test/`, the advisory mutation check ("temporarily make bin/csv2json.js ignore --tsv") and the flag-position probe. Step 4 of the builder brief lists only the commands the expect lines and proofs name, for example `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv; echo "exit=$?"`, plus `npm test`. These are allowed. Step 2 has the builder write its own tests using the expect-line inputs and outputs, which is also allowed. The builder brief contains no "PASS:" or "FAIL:" wording. The acceptance lines repeat the issue's expect lines, so they set the bar rather than describe how it will be checked.
